# ARCS: Towards Precise Text-to-SQL via Structured Disambiguation

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#arcs)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.09396v2) · arXiv:2610.09396v2, 14 October 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 29 pages: sections 1–6 and appendices A–E, annotation guidelines, schemas, query/data examples, agent/simulator prompts, model tables and eight-person user study; rendered taxonomy/statistics/schema figures inspected.

## Research question

Database questions can contain several interacting semantic, syntactic, schema and computation choices that conversational clarification handles inefficiently.

## Method

Structured disambiguation decomposes choices into multiple-choice selectors and threshold sliders. GPT-4.1 proposes questions over six existing databases; authors select, revise and annotate interpretations. A two-stage user simulator identifies relevant ambiguity points before answering.

## Evaluation

Separate tasks measure ambiguity coverage, exact disambiguation and SQL accuracy with supplied resolutions. End-to-end scoring permits extra output columns and conditions intended queries on non-empty results. The main comparison uses simulator token-based effort; eight participants provide a separate, small within-subject interface evaluation.

## What the results support

Structured interaction achieves similar execution performance with lower simulated effort; participants report lower workload. Incorrect SQL and missed/wrong interpretations remain common. More reasoning helps some configurations but not uniformly.

## Limits and qualifications

Questions are generated and author-curated, not a natural user-log sample. Global conventions remove some choices from ambiguity scoring. Completeness is relative to annotations and LLM alignment. The manuscript inconsistently states 331 versus 311 task instances; benchmark releases must be pinned.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A useful multi-ambiguity and interface benchmark whose finite choices, numeric vagueness, simulator assumptions and modest human evidence should remain explicit.
